overview: Randomised comparison of a structured validation checklist with usual validation, with duty days allocated in random permuted blocks of four within month, January to June 2027.
population: All syndromic surveillance alerts generated on study days; alerts arriving on a day are validated with that day's procedure.
exposure: Checklist days: the surveillance system opens the checklist form with each alert and requires the escalation rule to be recorded. Usual days: the form is hidden and validation proceeds as now.
procedures: The allocation list is held by an analyst outside the rota and released each morning. Time stamps for alert generation and the validation decision are taken from the system log. Outbreak reports up to 30 days later classify alerts as true or false events. A safety panel reviews every true event dismissed at the first alert within one week.

outcomes.name: Time to validation decision
outcomes.measure: Minutes from alert generation to the recorded validation decision, from system time stamps
outcomes.why: The efficiency the director asked about, responsive to structured validation (claim c1).

outcomes.name: True events dismissed at the first alert
outcomes.measure: Alerts later linked to a confirmed outbreak within 14 days that were dismissed at first validation, each reviewed by the safety panel
outcomes.why: The harm the checklist must not increase (claim c5).

outcomes.name: Escalations per 100 alerts
outcomes.measure: Alerts escalated to local health units
outcomes.why: Workload passed on to local units.

outcomes.name: Checklist completion
outcomes.measure: Proportion of alerts on checklist days with every check recorded
outcomes.why: Separates a weak checklist from one that was not used.

outcomes.name: Contamination
outcomes.measure: Usual-day validations whose free-text notes cite checklist items

feasibility: About 890 alerts over 180 duty days; no new staff; the form change is a configuration in the surveillance system.
biasMitigation: Day-level allocation concealed until each morning
Outcome from system time stamps, not self-report
Outbreak classification by staff unaware of the day's allocation

biasFlags.label: Contamination between procedures
biasFlags.note: Reduced by day allocation and measured monthly.

biasFlags.label: Few true events
biasFlags.note: Missed events cannot be compared statistically; case review instead.

flags: Adjustment for syndrome and weekday only
parsimony.simplestPath: One allocation unit, one time outcome, one safety review.

summary: Day-randomised comparison over six months with time to decision as primary outcome and case review of dismissed true events.
